text: {"claims": [{"id": "c1", "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S0", "rel": "entails"}, {"sid": "P2.S1", "rel": "entails"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P1.S0 states the 64-table join limit; P2.S1 states no mechanism exists to raise or lower the join-table limit, so sqlite3_limit() cannot change it."}, {"id": "c3", "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S2", "rel": "entails"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P4.S2 says with SQLITE_MAX_EXPR_DEPTH 0 the sqlite3_limit(...EXPR_DEPTH...) call is a no-op, matching the claim."}, {"id": "c6", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "The ~2e+13 rows figure is tied to a 281 terabyte database (max page size), not the default 4096-byte page size giving 17.5 TB; the claim misattributes it, so it is not supported."}, {"id": "c7", "evidence": [{"sid": "P5.S2", "rel": "entails"}, {"sid": "P5.S3", "rel": "entails"}], "check": {"kind": "arith", "expr": "281 / 17.5", "op": "==", "value": "16"}, "reasoning": "P5.S2 gives ~17.5 TB at 4096 bytes and P5.S3 gives ~281 TB at 65536 bytes; the size ratio matches the page-size ratio of 16, so both sentences are needed."}, {"id": "c8", "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S3", "rel": "refutes"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P7.S3 says more commonly applications want much lower limits, and P7.S2 calls increases rare, contradicting the claim that most need higher limits."}]}
